topics.title: Booking totals
topics.question: Do room charges reconcile to the claimed booking total?
flags: A dashboard headline includes amounts absent from the ledger.
topics.action: Reconcile individual room charges before discussing return.
topics.limit: A numerical match does not verify the transactions.
checks: Reconcile individual room charges before discussing return.

topics.title: Payout reconciliation
topics.question: Can gross bookings be bridged to cash paid out?
flags: Gross revenue is compared directly with a net bank receipt.
topics.action: Create a bridge for fees, refunds, taxes and timing.
topics.limit: Cash receipt and earned revenue are different measures.
checks: Create a bridge for fees, refunds, taxes and timing.

topics.title: Cleaning pass-through
topics.question: Are cleaning receipts and cleaning costs both visible?
flags: Cleaning income is included while the related expense is omitted.
topics.action: Show room revenue and cleaning economics separately.
topics.limit: A cleaning fee is not automatically profit.
checks: Show room revenue and cleaning economics separately.

topics.title: Refund adjustments
topics.question: Were cancellations and refunds incorporated consistently?
flags: Cancelled bookings remain in an earned-revenue total.
topics.action: Reconcile booked, completed, refunded and paid transactions.
topics.limit: Cancellation terms and accounting treatment require their own review.
checks: Reconcile booked, completed, refunded and paid transactions.

topics.title: Occupancy denominator
topics.question: Does the occupancy denominator use the stated availability?
flags: Booked nights are divided by fewer nights without explanation.
topics.action: Show total, available, blocked and booked nights separately.
topics.limit: High occupancy on limited availability need not mean high annual revenue.
checks: Show total, available, blocked and booked nights separately.

topics.title: Nightly rate average
topics.question: Is average nightly rate weighted by booked nights?
flags: A simple average of monthly rates differs from the annual weighted rate.
topics.action: Divide consistent room revenue by the booked nights it generated.
topics.limit: A weighted average still hides the distribution of rates.
checks: Divide consistent room revenue by the booked nights it generated.

topics.title: RevPAR definition
topics.question: Does revenue per available night use matching inputs?
flags: A per-booked-night figure is labeled as per-available-night revenue.
topics.action: Use matching revenue and availability for the same period.
topics.limit: RevPAR excludes costs and does not measure profit.
checks: Use matching revenue and availability for the same period.

topics.title: Partial-year annualization
topics.question: What does multiplying a partial period assume?
flags: A short high-demand period is multiplied into a full-year claim.
topics.action: Label the arithmetic and show the months not observed.
topics.limit: Annualization is an assumption rather than recorded annual performance.
checks: Label the arithmetic and show the months not observed.

topics.title: Seasonal mix
topics.question: Are strong months masking weak periods?
flags: Only the best quarter is visible in the summary.
topics.action: Compare full-cycle totals with the selected-period presentation.
topics.limit: Past monthly patterns do not establish future demand.
checks: Compare full-cycle totals with the selected-period presentation.

topics.title: Comparable selection bias
topics.question: Were inclusion rules defined before selecting examples?
flags: Only unusually strong properties remain in the comparison set.
topics.action: Document how each comparable was included or excluded.
topics.limit: Comparable data is not a property-specific forecast.
checks: Document how each comparable was included or excluded.

topics.title: Management fee base
topics.question: What amount is the management percentage applied to?
flags: The same percentage produces different dollar fees because the base differs.
topics.action: Apply the agreed definition to a transparent revenue base.
topics.limit: Only the current contract establishes the actual billing basis.
checks: Apply the agreed definition to a transparent revenue base.

topics.title: Platform charges
topics.question: Which platform fees are included in the projection?
flags: A single fee percentage is applied to channels with different treatment.
topics.action: Separate each channel's assumed revenue and charges.
topics.limit: Platform terms can change; confirm the current applicable schedule.
checks: Separate each channel's assumed revenue and charges.

topics.title: Utility schedule
topics.question: Does the annual utility cost include all modeled months?
flags: A low-season bill is multiplied by twelve without context.
topics.action: Show monthly observations and mark estimated months.
topics.limit: A prior owner's use may not match rental operations.
checks: Show monthly observations and mark estimated months.

topics.title: Insurance estimate
topics.question: Is the cost based on a quote for the intended use?
flags: An old premium is substituted for a current rental-use quote.
topics.action: Record the quote scope and ask the insurer about unresolved items.
topics.limit: This audit does not determine coverage or adequate insurance.
checks: Record the quote scope and ask the insurer about unresolved items.

topics.title: Property tax estimate
topics.question: Which basis and period support the tax cost used?
flags: A seller's historic payment is treated as a guaranteed buyer expense.
topics.action: Identify the source and ask the relevant authority or adviser about assumptions.
topics.limit: No tax calculation or jurisdiction-specific advice is provided.
checks: Identify the source and ask the relevant authority or adviser about assumptions.

topics.title: Repair allowance
topics.question: Does the repair amount cover the reported scope?
flags: A small allowance is shown while a larger scoped quote exists.
topics.action: Retain both values and request a reconciliation of scope and amount.
topics.limit: An allowance is not a contractor commitment.
checks: Retain both values and request a reconciliation of scope and amount.

topics.title: Reserve treatment
topics.question: Are reserve contributions distinguished from actual expenses?
flags: A reserve transfer is counted again as an expense when used.
topics.action: Keep earmarking, transfer and actual expenditure as separate events.
topics.limit: The appropriate accounting treatment needs professional review.
checks: Keep earmarking, transfer and actual expenditure as separate events.

topics.title: Capital work
topics.question: Is irregular capital work visible outside recurring expenses?
flags: A recurring-cost summary omits a known major project.
topics.action: Show timing and funding separately from normal operating costs.
topics.limit: This page does not decide capitalization or tax treatment.
checks: Show timing and funding separately from normal operating costs.

topics.title: Total cash invested
topics.question: Does the return denominator include the stated cash components?
flags: Only the down payment appears in a total-cash claim.
topics.action: Rebuild the denominator from documented components.
topics.limit: An agreed denominator still does not verify future cash flow.
checks: Rebuild the denominator from documented components.

topics.title: Deposit credits
topics.question: Is the deposit credited exactly once?
flags: A deposit is counted as both a new closing payment and an existing payment.
topics.action: Trace the deposit through the closing reconciliation.
topics.limit: Confirm final amounts with settlement professionals.
checks: Trace the deposit through the closing reconciliation.

topics.title: Purchase credits
topics.question: How do credits affect cash and price reporting?
flags: A credit reduces cash but is also subtracted again from purchase price.
topics.action: Show price, credits and cash requirement in separate fields.
topics.limit: Credit use depends on the actual transaction and financing terms.
checks: Show price, credits and cash requirement in separate fields.

topics.title: Fee timing
topics.question: When does each service or transaction charge become payable?
flags: A projected fee is excluded because it was paid before closing.
topics.action: Include the relevant committed cash regardless of payment date.
topics.limit: The agreement determines actual obligations and refund terms.
checks: Include the relevant committed cash regardless of payment date.

topics.title: Loan payment
topics.question: Does the modeled payment match the loan structure?
flags: Interest-only and amortizing payment figures are compared as equivalents.
topics.action: Recalculate the stated structure and list omitted payment components.
topics.limit: The worksheet is not a loan quote or approval.
checks: Recalculate the stated structure and list omitted payment components.

topics.title: Interest-only period
topics.question: Which periods use interest-only versus amortizing payments?
flags: The initial lower payment is applied to every future year.
topics.action: Show separate periods and identify the terms needed for later payments.
topics.limit: Do not infer later payments from the initial payment alone.
checks: Show separate periods and identify the terms needed for later payments.

topics.title: Balloon balance
topics.question: Is a future principal payment disclosed in the scenario?
flags: A balloon obligation is absent from a cash-flow narrative.
topics.action: Record the obligation and avoid treating refinancing as guaranteed.
topics.limit: Future refinancing availability is not established here.
checks: Record the obligation and avoid treating refinancing as guaranteed.

topics.title: Debt-service ratio
topics.question: Do NOI and debt service cover the same period?
flags: A monthly debt number divides annual income.
topics.action: Normalize the periods before calculating the ratio.
topics.limit: A modeled ratio does not establish lender eligibility.
checks: Normalize the periods before calculating the ratio.

topics.title: Return denominator
topics.question: Which cash base produces the stated return?
flags: The stated percentage uses a smaller denominator than the summary implies.
topics.action: Show the alternative calculations with explicit cash definitions.
topics.limit: No denominator choice turns a projection into a verified outcome.
checks: Show the alternative calculations with explicit cash definitions.

topics.title: Cash flow definition
topics.question: Which costs sit between revenue and the claimed cash flow?
flags: Operating income is labeled as spendable owner cash.
topics.action: Build the bridge from room revenue to operating income and then debt-adjusted cash.
topics.limit: Income tax and irregular costs may require additional treatment.
checks: Build the bridge from room revenue to operating income and then debt-adjusted cash.

topics.title: Projected versus actual
topics.question: Can a reader distinguish a model from an observed result?
flags: Projected income appears beside actual purchase costs without a label.
topics.action: Label every field historical, quoted, assumed or unresolved.
topics.limit: Combining observed and assumed fields creates a scenario, not a verified return.
checks: Label every field historical, quoted, assumed or unresolved.

topics.title: Reporting period
topics.question: Do the figures cover matching start and end dates?
flags: Income from twelve months is compared with expenses from nine.
topics.action: Align the periods or explain the bridge.
topics.limit: A matching period does not eliminate missing transactions.
checks: Align the periods or explain the bridge.

topics.title: Client-stage context
topics.question: What stage of the service did the reviewer experience?
flags: A sales-call review is read as proof of long-term operating results.
topics.action: Keep the review's actual scope visible when drawing conclusions.
topics.limit: Do not infer a reviewer used services they did not describe.
checks: Keep the review's actual scope visible when drawing conclusions.

topics.title: Review chronology
topics.question: How does the review date relate to the described service?
flags: A later update is treated as a separate customer's experience.
topics.action: Read the sequence and preserve context when summarizing.
topics.limit: A timestamp alone does not authenticate a review.
checks: Read the sequence and preserve context when summarizing.

topics.title: Review specificity
topics.question: Which parts of a review describe observable events?
flags: Broad praise or criticism is converted into a specific financial claim.
topics.action: Distinguish the writer's statements from your own inference.
topics.limit: Do not invent supporting details or contact reviewers without authorization.
checks: Distinguish the writer's statements from your own inference.

topics.title: Review incentives
topics.question: Is a material review incentive or relationship disclosed?
flags: A possible relationship is asserted as fact without evidence.
topics.action: Record what is disclosed and leave unsupported relationships unresolved.
topics.limit: This guide does not determine a legal violation.
checks: Record what is disclosed and leave unsupported relationships unresolved.

topics.title: Company ownership
topics.question: Is the publisher's relationship to BNB clear?
flags: A company resource appears to be an independent assessment.
topics.action: Keep the ownership statement visible alongside evaluative material.
topics.limit: This journal is published by My BnB Accelerator, LLC.
checks: Keep the ownership statement visible alongside evaluative material.

topics.title: Complaint resolution
topics.question: What evidence shows whether a concern was addressed?
flags: An invitation to contact support is described as a completed resolution.
topics.action: Separate response, proposed action and documented completion.
topics.limit: Do not infer that silence proves either resolution or fault.
checks: Separate response, proposed action and documented completion.

topics.title: Scope exclusion
topics.question: Does a proposal explicitly exclude the disputed task?
flags: An expected task is absent from the signed scope.
topics.action: Compare the actual deliverables and request clarification of conflicts.
topics.limit: This is evidence organization, not interpretation of contractual rights.
checks: Compare the actual deliverables and request clarification of conflicts.

topics.title: Responsibility boundary
topics.question: Which provider is responsible for the observed issue?
flags: Acquisition support is assumed to include ongoing property management.
topics.action: Map the specific event to a named role and retained scope.
topics.limit: Responsibility disputes may need qualified professional advice.
checks: Map the specific event to a named role and retained scope.

topics.title: Marketing timestamp
topics.question: Was the claim current for the service being evaluated?
flags: A current offer is used to describe an earlier engagement.
topics.action: Record which version applied to the time being discussed.
topics.limit: An archived page does not by itself establish the agreement's terms.
checks: Record which version applied to the time being discussed.

topics.title: Source traceability
topics.question: Can another reader locate the underlying evidence?
flags: A summary links to a homepage instead of the record supporting it.
topics.action: Attach a precise non-sensitive source reference to each material claim.
topics.limit: A link's existence does not certify the source.
checks: Attach a precise non-sensitive source reference to each material claim.

references.title: Claim register
references.question: What makes a claim reviewable?
references.intro: A claim register records the exact statement, publisher, date and supporting source separately from your interpretation.
references.action: Break a compound sentence into individual claims so each can have its own evidence status.
references.limit: A plausible statement is not verified just because it sounds specific.

references.title: Evidence hierarchy
references.question: How should source types be distinguished?
references.intro: An original transaction record, a provider quote, a company summary and a personal review answer different questions. Identify the source type before comparing conclusions.
references.action: Use the record closest to the question being tested and note what that record does not cover.
references.limit: No universal source ranking replaces checking relevance and completeness.

references.title: Missing evidence
references.question: What should an unavailable record mean?
references.intro: Unavailable means the supporting material has not been examined. It is different from disproved and different from confirmed.
references.action: Record the request and preserve the unknown status until the specific evidence arrives.
references.limit: An unanswered request does not establish misconduct.

references.title: Conflicting evidence
references.question: How do you preserve a disagreement between sources?
references.intro: Two records can differ because of timing, definitions, scope or error. Keep both values and their provenance rather than silently choosing one.
references.action: Write the smallest question that would explain the discrepancy and identify who can answer it.
references.limit: A newer source does not automatically invalidate every earlier source.

references.title: Weighted averages
references.question: Why can two averages disagree?
references.intro: A simple average gives every observation equal weight. A weighted average gives more influence to observations with more relevant units, such as booked nights.
references.action: Retain both the values and their weights and show the calculation explicitly.
references.limit: A correctly weighted mean can still hide an important range.

references.title: Denominator discipline
references.question: Why does the denominator deserve its own review?
references.intro: A percentage cannot be interpreted without the base it divides. Returns, occupancy and fee percentages can change when that base changes.
references.action: Name the denominator in the label and record excluded units or cash components.
references.limit: Two percentages with different denominators are not directly comparable.

references.title: Period alignment
references.question: What does matching periods require?
references.intro: State the start date, end date and basis of each figure. Cash received during one period can include bookings earned in another.
references.action: Build a timing bridge for settlements, refunds and unpaid amounts when comparing reports.
references.limit: Matching dates alone does not prove that records are complete.

references.title: Gross-to-net bridge
references.question: How should a reader trace a headline total?
references.intro: A bridge lists the additions and deductions between a gross measure and a net measure. It makes hidden differences visible.
references.action: Keep fees, refunds, taxes and timing adjustments as separate labeled lines.
references.limit: A reconciliation describes arithmetic; it is not an audit opinion.

references.title: Selection effects
references.question: Why do selected examples need context?
references.intro: A set chosen for publication may differ from the full set of experiences. Readers need the selection rule before treating the examples as representative.
references.action: Ask which records were eligible and which were excluded, without inventing missing population data.
references.limit: A selection explanation does not establish a typical customer result.

references.title: Survivorship limits
references.question: What can absent outcomes hide?
references.intro: A collection may show only properties or customers still visible in the source. That can leave discontinued or incomplete experiences outside the picture.
references.action: Describe the visible sample and avoid assuming it includes every relevant outcome.
references.limit: Do not claim an unseen failure or success rate.

references.title: Causal claims
references.question: Does an improvement establish what caused it?
references.intro: An observed change can coincide with other changes in season, pricing, property condition or operations. Sequence alone does not isolate cause.
references.action: Identify plausible competing explanations and the comparison needed to test them.
references.limit: A case study is not automatically a controlled experiment.

references.title: Range reporting
references.question: When is a range more informative than a point?
references.intro: A point estimate can hide the spread of observations. A range can show variation, but it still needs a definition and sample context.
references.action: Label whether a range is observed, min-to-max, assumed or a stress interval.
references.limit: Do not describe an assumed range as a statistical confidence interval.

references.title: Outlier review
references.question: How should an unusually strong example be handled?
references.intro: An outlier may be a valid observation or a sign of a definition or record issue. Investigate rather than deleting it automatically.
references.action: Compare the source, scope and time period with the rest of the set and record why it differs.
references.limit: Unusual performance does not establish typical performance.

references.title: Revision trail
references.question: How should a corrected number be presented?
references.intro: A correction should retain the original value, updated value, date and reason so readers can understand the change.
references.action: Link the revised claim to the underlying record and update dependent totals.
references.limit: Replacing a number without its context makes later review harder.

references.title: Screenshot limitations
references.question: What is missing from a dashboard screenshot?
references.intro: A screenshot can omit filters, periods, definitions or adjustments. It may show an interface without exposing the underlying transaction set.
references.action: Request a dated export or enough context to identify what the screen measures.
references.limit: A screenshot is not automatically false, but it may support only a narrow conclusion.

references.title: Attribution boundaries
references.question: How do you avoid adding meaning to a quotation?
references.intro: A summary should distinguish what the writer explicitly said from what the publisher infers. Preserve material limits and context.
references.action: Use a source link and narrow paraphrase instead of assigning unspoken motives or results.
references.limit: Do not invent or materially alter customer feedback.

references.title: Negative review context
references.question: How should criticism be evaluated fairly?
references.intro: Apply the same questions about specificity, date, scope and evidence to positive and negative feedback.
references.action: Separate the concern, the response and any documented follow-up without assuming the outcome.
references.limit: A negative account alone does not establish that every customer had that experience.

references.title: External-platform context
references.question: What does an external review platform establish?
references.intro: A platform provides its own publication and moderation environment. Its labels and processes should be read in the platform's own context.
references.action: Link to the original account and avoid claiming independent verification beyond what the source establishes.
references.limit: A third-party location does not make every claim accurate.

references.title: Uncertainty language
references.question: How should a source gap change the conclusion?
references.intro: Use language that matches what was actually examined:documented, reported, assumed, unresolved or contradicted by a specific record.
references.action: Explain which missing item would materially change the conclusion.
references.limit: Avoid turning an unresolved question into an accusation or endorsement.

references.title: Reproducibility
references.question: Could another reader repeat the comparison?
references.intro: A reproducible comparison needs input values, units, periods, formulas and source references. It should not depend on an unexplained spreadsheet output.
references.action: Save the assumptions beside the calculation and document any transformations.
references.limit: Reproducible arithmetic does not independently authenticate its inputs.
